title: Pascal Minus-One GCD
headline: Lean/Mathlib formalisation complete and Palomar verified; final source-level novelty audit complete, with paper preparation next.
description: This project studies $G(N;m)=\\gcd\\{\\binom Nk:0<k<N,\\ m\\mid k\\}$. The repository formally proves the $p\\equiv-1\\pmod m$ valuation theorem, the complementary $p\\equiv1\\pmod m$ branch, a common prime-power scaling theorem, and complete prime-by-prime valuation corollaries for $m=3,4,6$. The final source-level audit through 25 September 2026 located no equivalent prior theorem for the full minus-one classification. McTague's Theorem Q gives the plus-one branch, and the corrected arXiv v5 same-residue remark gives the one-parity minus-one branches for $p>m$; no equivalent prior theorem was located for the mixed-parity branch or the general $p=m-1$ regime. This is a negative-search statement rather than an unconditional historical-priority claim.
verification: Lean-verified theorem layer: minus-one valuation, plus-one valuation, scaling, and complete modulus 3, 4 and 6 valuation corollaries. Project Lean sources have zero explicit sorry, admit, or replacement axiom declarations; CI checks the build, regression tests, reference sweep, and zero-sorry gate. Palomar registry entry: PALOMAR-2026-09-25-000017, version 1.
attribution: John Fairfax-Ball maintains the repository and its Lean formalisation. Mathlib supplies Kummer's theorem and supporting digit machinery. McTague's 2017 work gives the plus-one theorem for the same restricted gcd family; the corrected arXiv v5 same-residue remark covers the one-parity minus-one branches for p>m and records the m=3, p=2 valuation-2 example. The final September 2026 audit located no equivalent prior theorem for the full minus-one classification, including no general treatment of the mixed-parity branch or the p=m-1 regime. Guo et al. (2026) formalised a different binomial-gcd family in Lean, so this project claims only that no equivalent formalisation of this restricted family was located.
